# The complete polynomial module generated by the bounded-source slabs

## Result and scope

Combining source slabs before clearing their common factors produces a
larger family than dividing each slab separately. For the five-letter,
weight-16 [bounded-source construction](bounded-source-dual-completion.md),
the full polynomial intersection of the rational slab span has a
degree-reduced basis with degrees

\[
 \boxed{0,0,0,8,8,8,12,16,16,16.}                         \tag{1}
\]

This is an all-degree module statement, proved by exact rational
reconstruction and a finite saturation certificate. It is not an
extrapolation from a degree scan.

Multiplying this module by `1+w` gives exactly its polynomial directions
that vanish at the crossing endpoint. At degree at most eighteen there
are 96 independent directions in a fixed first-label slab, hence
**480 independent full tensor directions** on five letters. Individual
generator normalization gave only 150 directions at that degree.

Every displayed direction can be added to any strict crossing on the
same five-letter alphabet. Its resulting complete profiles still require
evaluation. The module expansion itself does not improve the factoring
exponent, and it does not retain the original source-operator
interpretation after rational saturation.

## 1. The polynomial intersection to be computed

Let `K=F_2`, `R=K[w]`, and `F=K(w)`. The ten nonzero independent
bounded-source slabs are polynomial vectors `S_1,...,S_10` in `R^125`.
The coordinates are the physical triples `(y,u,v)`; the first logical
label is held fixed. Define

\[
 V=\operatorname{span}_F\{S_1,...,S_{10}\},\qquad
 M_{\rm sat}=V\cap R^{125}.                               \tag{2}
\]

Replacing a source slab by its primitive part does not change `V`.
Taking rational combinations can cancel polynomial factors shared
across several generators, so it can produce additional members of
`M_sat`.

The retained rational row reduction has rank ten. Its pivot columns,
in the slab order `y+5u+25v`, are

\[
 1,2,3,5,7,10,25,32,33,35.                               \tag{3}
\]

Write `H_1,...,H_10` for its reduced rows. The data include the exact
rational transformation from the original source slabs to these rows.
Every denominator is retained and checked.

## 2. A complete bounded-degree calculation

Consider `f` in `V` whose coordinates are polynomials of degree at most
`d`. Its reduced-row expansion is unique:

\[
 f=\sum_i a_i(w)H_i(w).                                  \tag{4}
\]

At pivot column `p_i`, equation (4) reads `f_(p_i)=a_i`. Therefore the
coefficients `a_i` are themselves polynomials of degree at most `d`.
There is no need to guess a denominator bound for the coefficients of
the original source generators.

For each coordinate `j`, choose a common denominator `D_j` for the ten
entries `H_(i,j)` and write `H_(i,j)=A_(i,j)/D_j`. Expand each unknown
`a_i` in degrees zero through `d`. Exact division of

\[
 \sum_i a_iA_{i,j}=D_j q_j+r_j                          \tag{5}
\]

gives linear equations requiring `r_j=0` and every coefficient of `q_j`
above degree `d` to vanish. These conditions are necessary and sufficient
for that coordinate to be a polynomial of degree at most `d`.

All equations are binary. Their nullspace is exactly

\[
 (M_{\rm sat})_{\le d}=\{f\in M_{\rm sat}:\deg f\le d\}.
 \tag{6}
\]

The constructor solves (5) for increasing degrees and retains a vector
only when it is independent of all polynomial shifts of the already
retained vectors. It produces the ten rows in (1).

Their leading coefficient vectors have rank ten. Consequently every
nonzero polynomial combination satisfies the predictable-degree identity

\[
 \deg\left(\sum_i c_i g_i\right)
   =\max_{i:c_i\ne0}(\deg c_i+\deg g_i).                  \tag{7}
\]

Indeed, the terms of maximal displayed degree have independent leading
vectors, so they cannot cancel.

## 3. A finite certificate proves saturation at every degree

The following elementary lemma avoids an unbounded denominator search.

**Degree-cutoff saturation lemma.** Let `g_1,...,g_r` be polynomial
vectors of degree at most `d`, let `M=sum_i R g_i`, and let
`V=span_F M`. If every polynomial vector in `V` of degree at most
`d-1` belongs to `M`, then `M=V cap R^n`.

**Proof.** Suppose a polynomial vector `v` belongs to the rational span
but not to `M`. Clearing its coefficients gives a nonzero polynomial
`f` with `fv in M`; choose one of least degree. It cannot be constant.
For an irreducible factor `p` of `f`, set `u=(f/p)v`. Minimality gives
`u notin M` and `pu in M`.

Write `pu=sum_i a_i g_i`, and divide `a_i=p b_i+r_i` with
`deg r_i<deg p`. Then

\[
 p\left(u-\sum_i b_i g_i\right)=\sum_i r_i g_i.            \tag{8}
\]

The vector in parentheses is polynomial, belongs to `V`, and is outside
`M`. Its degree is at most
`max_i(deg r_i+deg g_i)-deg p<=d-1`, contradicting the hypothesis.
This proves the lemma. **End of proof.**

For the present rows, `d=16`. The exact degree-fifteen system has 160
variables and rank 84, hence a 76-dimensional solution space. The
polynomial shifts of the displayed rows through degree fifteen also
give 76 independent vectors, by (7). Thus they exhaust (6) at degree
fifteen, and the lemma proves

\[
 \boxed{M_{\rm sat}=\bigoplus_{i=1}^{10}R g_i.}          \tag{9}
\]

The same certificate works over every characteristic-two extension
field. All equation ranks and leading-vector ranks are binary ranks,
which are unchanged by scalar extension. The saturation lemma then
applies over that extended field as well.

## 4. Exact endpoint-zero dimensions

By (7)--(9), the dimension at every degree is

\[
 \dim_K(M_{\rm sat})_{\le d}
   =\sum_{i=1}^{10}\max(0,d-\delta_i+1),                 \tag{10}
\]

where the `delta_i` are the degrees in (1).

A polynomial vector vanishes at `w=1` exactly when all its coordinates
are divisible by `1+w`. Division by that scalar keeps the vector in
the rational space `V`. Therefore the complete endpoint-zero submodule
is exactly

\[
 M_0=(1+w)M_{\rm sat}.                                  \tag{11}
\]

Its displayed primitive degrees are

\[
 1,1,1,9,9,9,13,17,17,17.                               \tag{12}
\]

Each primitive can be placed independently at any of the five first
logical labels. Those five slabs have disjoint supports. This gives
the following exact tensor dimensions:

| Maximum polynomial degree | Complete endpoint-zero tensor dimension |
| ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 15 |
| 9 | 150 |
| 13 | 275 |
| 16 | 380 |
| 17 | 430 |
| 18 | 480 |

The constant part of `M_sat` has dimension three. One basis vector is
the twenty-entry identity-mode support from the preceding note. The
other two have 24 nonzero coordinates each and are independent modulo
that identity-mode direction. Thus already at degree one there are
two additional scalar support tensors per first label.

## 5. Construction records and exact controls

The [constructor](../tools/source_slab_module_saturation.py) retains the
rational reduced basis, its transformation from the literal source
slabs, the polynomial module basis, and the saturation dimension
certificate. Its [direction record](../evidence/source-slab-module-directions-h16.json)
is directly usable by the prescribed-direction F4 row-lattice adapter.
The record includes all 480 degree-eighteen direction descriptors.

```sh
python3 tools/source_slab_module_saturation.py \
  evidence/bounded-dual-completion-h16.json --degree 18 \
  --output /tmp/source-slab-module-directions-h16.json
python3 tools/check_source_slab_module_saturation.py
```

The [checker](../tools/check_source_slab_module_saturation.py) verifies
1,250 exact rational reconstruction entries, all polynomial generator
memberships, the ten independent leading vectors, and the complete
degree-fifteen certificate. It also checks several other bounded-degree
dimensions through degree twenty and all endpoint-zero primitive
coefficients. Its negative controls reject an altered nonpivot
coordinate and a missing top-degree generator, and distinguish rational
reduced rows from a polynomial module basis.

The [exact verification record](../evidence/source-slab-module-saturation-checks.json)
contains the source hash, ranks, degrees, and complete dimension counts.

Separate finite row-frame searches can use these directions around the
existing five-letter reflection reference. They must retain the complete
coefficient degree, both physical cuts, and the charged paired types.
A finite target schedule and floating objective have a separate scope
from (9)--(12); a failed target search is not an exclusion of the
polynomial module at all frames.

The proof and implementation used substantial OpenAI assistant support.
No Lean source was changed and no improved factoring exponent is claimed.
